questions.question: A can do a piece of work alone in 10 days, whereas B alone can do it in 15 days. They work together and get Rs. 2000 for their work. What is the share of B?
questions.solution:
A = 10 days, B = 15 days

⇒ A : B = 10 : 15 = 2 : 3

We know, efficiency ∝ 1/Time

⇒ A : B = 3 : 2

⇒ Share of B = [2/ (2 + 3)] × 2000 = 2 × 400 = 800

∴ The share of B is Rs. 800

questions.question: If Anand can do a piece of work in 9 days and Vinod can complete the same work in 6 days, then in how many days will both of them complete it together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Anand can do a piece of work in 9 days.

Vinod can complete the same work in 6 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate = 1 / Number of days

Combined work rate = Sum of individual work rates

Time to complete work together = 1 / Combined work rate

**Calculation:**

Anand's work rate = 1 / 9

Vinod's work rate = 1 / 6

Combined work rate = (1 / 9) + (1 / 6)

⇒ Combined work rate = (2 + 3) / 18

⇒ Combined work rate = 5 / 18

Time to complete work together = 1 / (5 / 18)

⇒ Time to complete work together = 18 / 5

**The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: Anjali and Manju together can do a piece of work in 5 days. If Anjali does twice as much work as Manju in a given time, how long would Anjali alone take to do the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Anjali and Manju together can do a piece of work in 5 days.

Anjali does twice as much work as Manju in a given time.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by Anjali and Manju together in 1 day = 1 / Total days

Work done by Anjali alone in 1 day = 2 × Work done by Manju alone in 1 day

Let the work done by Manju alone in 1 day be M.

Then, the work done by Anjali alone in 1 day = 2M.

Work done by Anjali and Manju together in 1 day = 2M + M = 3M .

Since they can complete the work together in 5 days,

Work done by Anjali and Manju together in 1 day = 1/5

**Calculation:**

3M = 1/5

⇒ M = 1/(5 × 3)

⇒ M = 1/15

Therefore, the work done by Anjali alone in 1 day = 2M = 2 × 1/15 = 2/15

Number of days required by Anjali alone to complete the work = 1 / (2/15)

⇒ Number of days = 15 / 2

⇒ Number of days = 7.5

**Anjali alone would take 7.5 days to do the work.**

questions.question: S can do a piece of work in 80 days and T in 60 days. With help of U, they finish the work in 20 days. In how many days U alone can do the same work?
questions.solution:
Work done by S in one day = 1/80

Work done by T in one day = 1/60

Let work done by U in one day = 1/x

Work done by all three in one day = 1/20

Now, 1/80 + 1/60 + 1/x = 1/20

1/x = 5/240

∴ Number of days required by U to finish the work = x = 240/5 = 48 days

questions.question: 14 workers working 16 hours per day can demolish a building in 81 days. In how many days 18 workers working 24 hours per day can demolish the same building?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct MDH formula: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

⇒ 14 × 81 × 16 = 18 × D₂ × 24

⇒ D₂ = (14 × 81 × 16) ÷ (18 × 24)

⇒ D₂ = 18144 ÷ 432

⇒ D₂ = 42 days

**∴ The correct answer is 42 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Workers in first group (M₁) = 14

Days taken (D₁) = 81

Hours per day (H₁) = 16

Workers in second group (M₂) = 18

Hours per day (H₂) = 24

**Formula Used:**

Since the building to be demolished is the same, the total work is constant (W₁ = W₂).

MDH Rule: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

 
 Group 1
 14 M × 81 D × 16 H
 
 =
 
 
 Group 2
 18 M × D × 24 H

**Calculation:**

⇒ 14 × 81 × 16 = 18 × D₂ × 24

⇒ D₂ = (14 × 81 × 16) ÷ (18 × 24)

Simplifying the ratios step-by-step:

⇒ D₂ = 14 × (81 ÷ 18) × (16 ÷ 24)

⇒ D₂ = 14 × (9 ÷ 2) × (2 ÷ 3)

Canceling out the common factor of 2:

⇒ D₂ = 14 × (9 ÷ 3)

⇒ D₂ = 14 × 3

⇒ D₂ = 42 days

**∴ The correct answer is 42 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

The rule states that if M₁ persons can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours a day, and M₂ persons can do W₂ work in D₂ days working H₂ hours a day, then (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Work Equivalence Principle

When two groups perform the exact same task, the total effort measured in man-hours or man-days remains constant. Thus, Total Work = Men × Days × Hours.

Direct and Inverse Proportions

More work requires more workers (direct proportion, M ∝ W). More workers require fewer days to complete the same work (inverse proportion, M ∝ 1 ÷ D).
</p

questions.question: A factory requires 56 machines to manufacture a given number of articles in 144 days. How many machines will be required to produce the same number of articles in 96 days?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Number of machines = 56

Days = 144

**Formula Used:**

(M1 times D1)/(W1) = (M2 times D2)/(W2) 

M = Men/Machines

D = Days 

W = Work

**Calculation:**

M₁ = 56

D₁ = 144

D₂ = 96

W₁ = W₂

 (M1 times D1)/(W1) = (M2 times D2)/(W2) 

⇒ (56 times 144)/(W) = (M2 times 96)/(W) 

⇒ M₂ = 84 

**∴ 84 machines to be required**

questions.question: 40 mechanics can repair a bike in 56 days. In how many days 32 mechanics will do the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the chain rule (M₁D₁ = M₂D₂):

⇒ 40 × 56 = 32 × D₂

⇒ D₂ = (40 × 56) ÷ 32

⇒ D₂ = 2240 ÷ 32 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Assuming the efficiency of 1 mechanic is 1 unit/day.

⇒ Total Work = Efficiency of 40 Mechanics × Days

⇒ Total Work = 40 × 56 = 2240 units

⇒ Days required by 32 Mechanics = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of 32 Mechanics

⇒ Days = 2240 ÷ 32

⇒ Days = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Formula)

(M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M is Men, D is Days, H is Hours, and W is Work.

Inverse Proportion

When the amount of work is constant, the number of workers is inversely proportional to the number of days required (M × D = Constant). More mechanics will take fewer days, and fewer mechanics will take more days.

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 25 days and 55 days, respectively. The total number of days (in whole number) to complete the work, if A and B both work together, is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 25 days.

B can complete the work in 55 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A and B together in one day = (1 / A's time) + (1 / B's time)

Total time to complete the work = 1 / (Work done by A and B together in one day)

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in one day = 1 / 25

Work done by B in one day = 1 / 55

Work done by A and B together in one day = (1 / 25) + (1 / 55)

⇒ Work done by A and B together in one day = (1)/(25) + (1)/(55)

⇒ Work done by A and B together in one day = (55 + 25)/(25 × 55)

⇒ Work done by A and B together in one day = (80)/(1375)

⇒ Work done by A and B together in one day = (16)/(275)

Total time to complete the work = 1 / ((16)/(275))

⇒ Total time to complete the work = (275)/(16)

⇒ Total time to complete the work = 17.1875 days

Rounding to the whole number, total time = 18 days

**The total number of days to complete the work if A and B both work together is 18 days.**

questions.question: If 27 men take 15 days to mow 225 hectares of grass, how long will 33 men take to mow 165 hectares?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

27 men take 15 days to mow 225 hectares.

Number of men = 33

Area = 165 hectares

**Formula used:**

Work = Men × Days

Men × Days (1) ÷ Area (1) = Men × Days (2) ÷ Area (2)

**Calculations:**

(27 × 15) ÷ 225 = (33 × Days) ÷ 165

⇒ (405) ÷ 225 = (33 × Days) ÷ 165

⇒ 1.8 = (33 × Days) ÷ 165

⇒ Days = (1.8 × 165) ÷ 33

⇒ Days = 297 ÷ 33

⇒ Days = 9

**∴ 33 men will take 9 days to mow 165 hectares.**

questions.question: U, V and W together can complete a work in 10 days. If U alone can complete the work in 20 days and V alone can complete the work in 30 days, then in how many days W alone can complete the work?
questions.solution:
1 day work of U, V and W = 1/10

1 day work of U = 1/20

1 day work of V = 1/30(3)

⇒ 1 day work of W = (1/10) - (1/20) - (1/30) = 1/60

∴ W can complete the work in 60 days.

questions.question: R can do a work in 90 days. What percent work of the total work can be done by R in 45 days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

R can complete the work in 90 days.

**Formula Used:**

Percentage of work done = (Days worked / Total days to complete work) × 100

**Calculation:**

Days worked = 45

Total days to complete work = 90

Percentage of work done = (45 / 90) × 100

⇒ Percentage of work done = 0.5 × 100

⇒ Percentage of work done = 50%

**The correct answer is option 2: 50 percent.**

questions.question: 40 persons can repair a bridge in 12 days. If 8 more persons join them, then in how many days bridge can be repaired?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

40 persons can repair a bridge in 12 days

Concept:

Work = Total manpower × Total days

M1D1/W1 = M2D2/W2

**Calculation:**

M₁ = 40, D₁ = 12, M₂ = 48, D₂ = y (Let)

Using the formula

M1D1/W1 = M2D2/W2

⇒ 40 × 12 = 48 × y

⇒ y = (40 × 12/48) = 10

**∴ 48 persons can repair a bridge in 10 days.**

questions.question: Twenty persons take 15 days to complete a certain work. working 8 hours a day. To complete the same work in 4 days, working 10 hours a day, the number of persons required is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Twenty persons take 15 days to complete a certain work. working 8 hours a day.

Later, the same work is to be completed in 4 days, working 10 hours a day.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency of each worker × Number of Hours × Number of days to finish × Number of total workers

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of each worker be Q units a day and the number of required workers to finish the work in 4 days be N.

According to the question,

Q × 8 × 15 × 20 = Q × 10 × 4 × N

⇒ N = 60

**∴ To complete the same work in 4 days, working 10 hours a day, the number of persons required is 60.**

questions.question: Sunil and Pradeep can complete a work in 5 days and 15 days, respectively. They both work for one day and then Sunil leaves. In how many days is the remaining work completed by Pradeep?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sunil can complete the work in 5 days.

Pradeep can complete the work in 15 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate of Sunil = 1/5

Work rate of Pradeep = 1/15

**Calculation:**

Work done by Sunil in 1 day = 1/5

Work done by Pradeep in 1 day = 1/15

Work done by both in 1 day = (1/5) + (1/15)

⇒ Work done by both in 1 day = (1)/(5) + (1)/(15)

⇒ Work done by both in 1 day = (3 + 1)/(15)

⇒ Work done by both in 1 day = (4)/(15)

Remaining work after 1 day = 1 - (4)/(15)

⇒ Remaining work = (15)/(15) - (4)/(15)

⇒ Remaining work = (11)/(15)

Time taken by Pradeep to complete the remaining work = Remaining work / Work rate of Pradeep

⇒ Time = (11/15)/(1/15)

⇒ Time = 11 days

**The remaining work is completed by Pradeep in 11 days.**

questions.question: Pankaj is 40 percent less efficient than Rahul. If Rahul can make a computer in 16 days, then Pankaj can make the same computer in how many days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pankaj is 40% less efficient than Rahul.

**Formula Used:**

Time taken by Pankaj = Time taken by Rahul × (1 + Efficiency reduction factor)

**Calculation:**

Efficiency reduction factor = 40% = 0.40

Efficiency of Rahul = 100%

Efficiency of Pankaj = 100% - 40% = 60% = 0.60

Time taken by Rahul = 16 days

Let TPₐₙₖₐj be the time taken by Pankaj.

Since Pankaj is 60% as efficient as Rahul, he will take more time to complete the same task.

Time taken by Pankaj is given by:

TPₐₙₖₐj = frac{TRₐₕᵤₗ}{EfficiencyPₐₙₖₐj}

⇒ 16/0.60 

⇒1600/60

⇒ 80/3

**The time taken by Pankaj to make the same computer is 80/3 days.**

questions.question: Z1, Z2 and Z3 can do a work in 100, 50 and 75 days respectively. All three of them began the work together but Z2 left 15 days before the completion of the work. In how many days was the work completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Z1 can do the work in 100 days.

Z2 can do the work in 50 days.

Z3 can do the work in 75 days.

Z2 left 15 days before the completion of the work.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate of Z1 = 1/100

Work rate of Z2 = 1/50

Work rate of Z3 = 1/75

Total work done = Work rate × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the total time taken to complete the work be T days.

Z2 worked for (T - 15) days.

Work done by Z1 in T days = T × (1/100)

Work done by Z2 in (T - 15) days = (T - 15) × (1/50)

Work done by Z3 in T days = T × (1/75)

Total work done = 1 (since the whole work is completed)

⇒ T/100 + (T - 15)/50 + T/75 = 1

⇒ T/100 + (T/50 - 15/50) + T/75 = 1

⇒ T/100 + T/50 - 15/50 + T/75 = 1

⇒ T/100 + 2T/100 - 15/50 + 4T/300 = 1

⇒ 3T/100 - 15/50 + 4T/300 = 1

⇒ 3T/100 - 3/10 + 4T/300 = 1

⇒ 9T/300 + 4T/300 - 3/10 = 1

⇒ 13T/300 - 3/10 = 1

⇒ 13T/300 = 1 + 3/10

⇒ 13T/300 = 10/10 + 3/10

⇒ 13T/300 = 13/10

⇒ 13T = 39

⇒ T = 30

**The work was completed in 30 days.**

questions.question: A, B and C can complete a work in 5, 10 and 30 days respectively. In how many days A, B and C together can complete the same work?

Hence, A + B + C can complete the whole work in 3 days.

questions.question: If Y can complete (3)/(5) of a work in 60 days, then Y will complete(1)/(10) of the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Y completes 3/5 of the work in 60 days.

We need to find the time Y takes to complete 1/10 of the same work.

**Formula used:**

Time to complete a fraction of work = (Time for given fraction × Required fraction) ÷ Given fraction

**Calculations:**

Time = (60 × 1/10) ÷ (3/5)

⇒ Time = (60 ÷ 10) ÷ (3 ÷ 5)

⇒ Time = 6 ÷ (3/5)

⇒ Time = 6 × (5/3)

⇒ Time = **10 days**

**∴ Y will take 10 days to complete 1/10 of the work.**

questions.question: A camp has provisions for 60 pupils for 18 days. In how many days will the same provisions finish off if the strength of the camp is increased to 72 pupils?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Provisions for 60 pupils for 18 days.

Strength increased to 72 pupils.

**Formula used:**

Total Provisions = Number of Pupils × Number of Days

**Calculations:**

Total Provisions = 60 × 18 = 1080 pupil-days

Let the number of days the provisions will last for 72 pupils be **d**.

Total Provisions = 72 × d

⇒ 72 × d = 1080

⇒ d = 1080 ÷ 72

⇒ d = 15

**Answer:**

The provisions will finish off in **15 days** if the strength is increased to 72 pupils.

questions.question: An experienced carpenter can complete a woodwork in 8 days. A young carpenter can complete the same work in 12 days. Both work together for 3 days, and then the latter leaves. How may days will be taken by the former to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Let total work = LCM of (8 and 12) = 24 units

Hence, the efficiency of experienced carpenter = 24/8 = 3 units/day

And, the efficiency of young carpenter = 24/12 = 2 units/day

Both work together for 3 days, work done = (3 + 2) × 3 = 15 units

Hence, remaining work = 24 – 15 = 9 units

Now, time taken for remaining work = frac{{Remaining work}}{{Efficiency of experienced carpenter}} 

⇒ time taken for remaining work {{ }} = (9)/({3 )} = 3 days

∴ Former carpenter will complete the remaining work in 3 days.

questions.question: A alone can make a chair in 40 days and B alone can make the same chair in 24 days. If A and B are working on alternate days and A works on the first day, then in how many days will the chair be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

A can make the chair in days = 40

B can make the same chair in days = 24

**Concept: **

In this type of question always imagine the total work as LCM of time taken by individuals to perform the work.

**Formula used: **

Efficiency = Total work/Time taken

**Calculation: **

Let the total work be LCM of 40, 24 i.e. 120 unit

Efficiency of A = 120/40 = 3 unit/day

Efficiency of B = 120/24 = 5 unit/day

If they work on alternate days starting from A their 2 days work

= 3 + 5 = 8 unit

i.e. 8 units of work completed in 2 days

So, (8 × 15) = 120 units of work be completed in (2 × 15) = 30 days

**∴ The chair will be completed in = 30 days**

questions.question: A is four times as good a workman as B and together they finish a piece of work in 84/15 days. In how many days can A alone finish the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A is four times as good a workman as B.

Together they finish a piece of work in (84)/(15) days.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate of A = 4 × Work rate of B

Combined work rate = Work rate of A + Work rate of B

Work rate = Work / Time

**Calculation:**

Let B's work rate be x. Then, A's work rate is 4x.

Combined work rate = x + 4x = 5x

Total work = Combined work rate × Time

Total work = 5x × (84)/(15)

Total work = 5x × (28)/(5)

Total work = 28x

Time taken by A alone to finish the work = Total work / Work rate of A

Time taken by A alone = (28x)/(4x)

Time taken by A alone = (28)/(4)

Time taken by A alone = 7 days

**A alone can finish the work in 7 days.**

questions.question: A, B and C are Accountants. A alone can file a return in 6 hours and B alone can file the same return in 10 hours. All three together can do it in 3 hours. In what time will C alone file the same return?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 6, 10, 3) = 30 units.

Efficiency: A = 30/6 = 5; B = 30/10 = 3; (A+B+C) = 30/3 = 10.

Efficiency of C = Total Efficiency − (A + B) = 10 − (5 + 3) = 2 units/hr.

Time for C = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hours.**

questions.question: P alone can complete a work in 15 days and Q alone can complete the same work in 12 days. They start the work together but after 3 days P leaves the work. How much time will Q take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(15, 12) = 60 units.

Efficiency of P = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units/day | Efficiency of Q = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units/day.

Work done together in 3 days = 3 × (4 + 5) = 27 units.

Remaining time for Q = (60 − 27) ÷ 5 = 33 ÷ 5 = 6.6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 15 days.

Time taken by Q to complete the work = 12 days.

P and Q work together for 3 days, then P leaves.

**Method Used:**

LCM Method: Total Work = LCM of individual days.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = 60 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P and Q = 4 + 5 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by P and Q in 3 days = 9 × 3 = 27 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 27 = 33 units.

⇒ Time taken by Q to finish the remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Q's efficiency.

⇒ Time taken by Q = 33 ÷ 5 = 6.6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fractional Work Method

If a person completes a job in x days, then the part of the work completed in 1 day is 1/x. Work remaining after n days is 1 − (n ÷ x).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by the individuals. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept of time and work directly applies to pipes and cisterns. Filling a tank is considered positive work, while emptying a tank is considered negative work.

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days, and B and C together can do the same work in 100 days. If B alone can do the same work in 140 days, then in how many days will A and C together can complete the same work?

B and C can do the same work in 100 days.

B alone can do the same work in 140 days.

Work done = Efficiency × Number of Days

⇒ Work done by (A + B) in a day = 1/20.

⇒ Work done by (B + C) in a day = 1/100.

⇒ Work done by B in a day = 1/140.

⇒ Work done by A in a day = (A + B
) - B = 1/20 - 1/140 = 6/140 = 3/70.

⇒ Work done by C in a day = (B + C) - B = 1/100 - 1/140 = 2/700 = 1/350.

⇒ Therefore, A and C together can do the work in 1/(A + C) = 1/(3/70 + 1/350) = 1/(4/70) = 175/8 days.

**Therefore, A and C together can complete the same work in 175/8 days.**

⇒ 25 days
